{{Short description|Position at the University of Manchester in England}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2025}}
The '''Richardson Chair of Applied Mathematics'''  is an endowed professorial position in the [[School of Mathematics, University of Manchester]], England. The chair was founded by an endowment of £3,600 from one  John Richardson,  in 1890. The endowment was originally used to support the Richardson Lectureship in Mathematics.<ref>{{citation|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0INPAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA54|title=The Owens College, Manchester (founded 1851); a Brief History of the College and Description of Its Various Departments|page=54|first=P. J.|last=Hartog|year=1900}}.</ref>
One holder of the Richardson Lectureship was [[John Edensor Littlewood]] (1907–1910).  The position lapsed in 1918, but was   resurrected as a lectureship in Pure Mathematics between 1935 and 1944. There was then a further hiatus until the establishment of the Richardson Chair of Applied Mathematics in 1998. The current holder (since 1998) is [[Nicholas Higham]].<ref>[http://www.manchester.ac.uk/research/Nick.higham/ Staff profile for Nicholas Higham], Univ. of Manchester, retrieved 27 June 2014.</ref>

A complete list of Richardson Lecturers and Professors is as follows:{{cn|date=June 2014}}
*F. T. Swanwick		        (1891–1907) Lecturer in Mathematics
*[[John Edensor Littlewood|J. E. Littlewood]]	(1907–1910) Lecturer in Mathematics
*H. R. Hasse			(1910–1912) Lecturer in Mathematics
*W. D. Evans			(1912–1918) Lecturer in Mathematics
*W. N. Bailey 			(1935–1944) Lecturer in Pure Mathematics
*[[Nicholas Higham|N. J. Higham]]		(1998–	)  Professor of Applied Mathematics

The School of Mathematics has three other endowed chairs, the others being the [[Beyer Chair of Applied Mathematics|Beyer Chair]], the [[Fielden Chair of Pure Mathematics]] and the [[Sir Horace Lamb Chair]].
